text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] cluster-gpu-2: runtime-serve-78 experiencing repeated OOMs and container restarts (5x in 12m). Node flaps reported. Auto-restart triggered. severity=P2. Suspected KV cache growth + paged-attention saturation.

Dana: I’m on it, picking up on-call. First glance shows /var/log/runtime OOM messages + recent CUDA driver noise.

Omar: I’m seeing steady growth in kv_cache.bytes_used on that node — no big evictions for ~3h. Eviction timer appears stuck.

Jess: Confirmed. The paged-attn allocator is holding onto stale pages; free lists are not releasing. Could be the eviction heartbeat didn’t run after a config rollout last night.

Liam: Any customer impact?

Dana: A few tenants are seeing 5-10% increased latency and occasional 503s when pods restart. No major data loss. Notifying SRE and CS.

Jess: Quick mitigation options: 1) force eviction on affected pods; 2) roll nodes (drain+replace) to reclaim memory; 3) temporarily route traffic to lower-capacity fallback model.

Omar: I can push a hotfix to the runtime flags to lower kv_cache.max_stale_age from 30m to 2m, and enable immediate compaction flag `--kv-compact-on-threshold`. This should free pages on next GC pass.

Dana: Do it. Also, set pod annotation `redwood/eviction=immediate` for runtime-serve-* on cluster-gpu-2 to trigger eviction loop.

Omar: Patching now. Pushing config to 3 pods first (canary).

infra-bot: deploy: config/runtime/kv-eviction-patch -> rollout started (3/12 pods).

Jess: While canary is rolling, I’ll increase observability: add kv_cache.bytes_used and paged_attn.free_pages to the dashboard, and create alert if free_pages < 100 for >2m.

Dana: CS update sent: "We’re mitigating an infrastructure memory issue affecting a small subset of requests. We’ve applied a targeted config change and are monitoring. We’ll follow up with root cause and timeline."

Omar: Canary results: canary pods show immediate drop in kv_cache.bytes_used (~18%) and free_pages rising. No OOMs in 6m. Rolling to remaining pods now.

infra-bot: deploy: config/runtime/kv-eviction-patch -> rollout 12/12 pods succeeded.

Liam: Node flaps continue? Observed two node restarts earlier but none since patch.

Jess: CUDA error spikes correlated with the time free_pages hit zero. I suspect paged-attn allocation requests hit a slow path and forced kernel thrash. Fixing page reclamation has reduced CUDA driver errors as well.

Dana: Live mitigation summary (to hand off):
- Action taken: pushed `--kv-compact-on-threshold` + lowered `kv_cache.max_stale_age`, annotated pods for immediate eviction, rolled config across cluster-gpu-2 (all pods).
- Observed effect: avg kv_cache.bytes_used down ~20%, paged_attn.free_pages back to nominal, OOM restarts stopped. Latency back to baseline for affected tenants.
- Customer impact: transient 503s and latency spikes during restarts (approx 15-20 minutes window); CS notified.
- Follow-ups: investigate why eviction heartbeat stopped after last night’s config rollout, write regression test for eviction timers, consider auto-safety that caps kv cache growth per pod.

Omar: I’ll open a PR with allocator metric instrumentation and a test for eviction heartbeats failing during rollout.

Jess: Also recommend a short-term alert: kv_cache.bytes_used > 85% of kv_cache.max triggers paging mitigation runbook.

Liam: For next on-call: monitor node flaps and CUDA error rate. If OOMs resume, escalate to Eng Runtime and consider immediate node replacement + isolate traffic via routing policy.

Dana: Handing off to @omar for follow-up and @jess for monitoring changes. If anything reoccurs, ping me directly.

omar: Acknowledged — will follow up with PR and postmortem draft.

jess: I’ve added the dashboard panels and alert. Linking runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/paged-attn-ooms

infra-bot: incident-note: incident created 1895006789. severity=P2. state=mitigated -> monitoring.

Dana: Thanks team. Closing thread for active mitigation; leave any postmortem notes here. :thumbsup:
